items.project_definition: A synchronization gate ensuring all blocking prerequisites are verified before parallel development of user stories commences.
The shared infrastructure layer containing core entity definitions and I/O helpers that blocks all subsequent feature implementation.
The high-level functional objective that a specific user story must satisfy to be considered complete.
A sequential alphanumeric token assigned to each task to ensure unique identification within the persistent store.
The lightweight data-interchange format used for persistent storage in ~/.todos.json and for machine-readable output.
The minimum set of functional capabilities, specifically adding and completing tasks, required for the first viable release.
The structural grouping of implementation units by user story to maintain independent testability.
The set of design documents including plan, spec, and data-model required before execution begins.
The primary documentation file detailing command-line usage and storage behavior.
The initial phase focused on project skeleton creation and pyproject.toml configuration.
The specific implementation unit responsible for handling empty-list scenarios in the user interface.
The verification suite divided into unit and integration directories to validate system behavior.
The process of assigning a timestamp to the created_at field during task instantiation.
The operational command that purges all entries marked as completed from the storage.
The operational command that retrieves and displays all stored entries in human-readable or machine-parseable formats.
A high-priority constraint indicating that no subsequent work can proceed until the current phase is fully validated.
